raw_response:
I'm 67 this year, been farming these 12 mu for 40 years. Never went to school, but this land taught me everything. My old man started this farm, and I took over when he couldn't work no more. I've got my wife with me, and my son works at the factory in town but comes back for harvest. We've got 8 mu in the north field that does wheat then maize, and 4 mu by the house in cotton. That's how we've always done it — cotton brings good money when the price holds, and wheat-maize keeps us fed and pays for the fertilizer.

The wheat went in last October, same week as always. I used my own seed, the local kind that's been here for years. Not fancy, but it doesn't get sick like those new hybrids. Back in March when the wheat started turning green, I spread urea — one big bag for every two mu, about 25 jin per mu. That's what my father did, that's what I do. Now it's getting warm, the wheat is tall. I'll irrigate it one more time before harvest if the sky stays dry — the pump costs money, about 20 yuan each time, so I watch the weather and don't water unless I have to. I'll cut it around June 10th with the combine I hire from Old Zhang in the village. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu, I hope for the same. I don't spray wheat much, maybe once for weeds if the chickweed gets bad.

Cotton is going in right now, late April. I bought new seed this year — my nephew down the road said this kind gives fat bolls, better than what I saved. Cost me about 30 yuan per mu. I put pig manure on that field last winter, good black stuff. When I plant, I put compound fertilizer in the furrow, about 30 jin per mu. Cotton needs water to get started, so I'll run the pump once after planting if it doesn't rain. Then once more in July when it flowers. The bollworm is trouble every year — I spray three times with the medicine from the co-op, about 30 yuan each time. Picking kills my back at my age. My wife and I do what we can, but I have to hire women from the village for the main pick — 100 yuan a day. I need about 5 days of help for the 4 mu.

Maize comes right after wheat, no rest! Around June 15th, as soon as the wheat is off and threshed. I hire Old Wang's tractor to plow quick, 50 yuan per mu. I buy hybrid maize seed, about 4 jin per mu, costs me about 40 yuan. At planting I put compound fertilizer and urea down together — about 50 jin of compound and 30 jin of urea per mu. If July is dry I'll irrigate once, maybe twice if it's bad. Maize is easier than cotton, doesn't need as much watching. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu.

Money is always tight. Fertilizer went up again at the shop. I spend about 4,200 yuan on all the seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, water, and hired help. I have to keep 2,000 yuan aside for my blood pressure medicine and emergencies — I'm not young anymore. My son sends some money from town, but I don't like to ask. I don't try new things — last year Liu from the east end tried some new wheat variety and it got rust bad. I'll stick with what I know. Better to put down a bit more fertilizer than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, and I've seen too many bad years.
